newsitem.title: USA: N.H. Senate hikes tobacco tax 12 cents a pack.
newsitem.headline: N.H. Senate hikes tobacco tax 12 cents a pack.

text.p: New Hampshire's Senate Tuesday killed Gov. Jeanne Shaheen's proposed 25 cent per pack increase of the state cigarette tax in favor of a 12 cent per pack hike.
Shaheen proposed a 25 cent hike to generate more than $60 million annually in additional revenue to help fund a $44 million budget deficit, new state programs and a statewide kindergarten plan.
Shaheen's proposal had been amended in the 400 member New Hampshire House down to 20 cents. The governor said at the time she could abide by the House compromise.
The American Cancer Society supported the governor's increase saying it would discourage underage smoker from starting by hiking the cost of a pack of cigarettes.

Senate Republicans said improving revenue figures from other state taxes, fees and liquor sales made a 25 cent per pack increase unnecessary to balance the state budget. They said increasing the current 25 cent per pack tax would hurt cross-border tobacco sales and cause small stores to lose business.
Sen. James Rubens, R-Etna, pushed through a kindergarten program Tuesday that Republicans claimed could be easily funded by a 12 cent per pack increase of the cigarette tax.
The Senate, led by its Republican majority, killed Shaheen's $50 million incentive aid and construction program for kindergarten.
Shaheen vowed to veto the Senate bill if it survived a House-Senate conference committee session.
The tobacco tax increase is also headed for a conference committee session.
